mainTopic: The 24-hour rule for lost produce set aside for tithes, רבי יהודה's set seasons, and an aggadic discussion of the winds.
overview: The גמרא finishes the dispute over whether the 24 hours (מעת לעת) are counted from the checking or from the setting aside. It shows that the משנה's wording is a difficulty (קשיא) for the setting-aside view. The אמורא רבי אלעזר then says that the תנא רבי אלעזר's colleagues disagree with his 24-hour rule. He proves it from a משנה about a מקוה found lacking, where 'למפרע' goes all the way back. On רבי יהודה's times for checking wine, a ברייתא explains that the east wind after סוכות must come in its usual season. A related ברייתא lists set selling times, which רבא explains are for partners. The east wind leads to a discussion of winds: the meaning of 'חרישית', גניבא's teaching about the north and south winds, and a story about רב נחמן בר יעקב and the harmful שַׁדְיָא wind. That discussion ends with three views drawn from one פסוק in הושע, and רבא begins explaining its opening words, a thought that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The second view: 24 hours from when it was set aside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes the second opinion in the dispute: the 24-hour window is counted from the time the produce or money was set aside.
steps.simpleTranslation: The second view says the 24 hours are counted from when it was set aside.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a dispute that started just before. One view says the 24 hours are counted from the checking, and this second view says they are counted from the setting aside (הנחה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this view, the person must worry about everything he relied on from 24 hours after he set the item aside until the moment he checked. The other view only makes him worry about the 24 hours right before the checking (בדיקה).

keyTerms.meaning: A full 24-hour period, from a given time until the same time on the next or previous day
Setting aside (here, putting aside produce or money to rely on for separating tithes)
Checking (here, the moment he checked and found the item gone)

phrases.english: A 24-hour period counted from the setting aside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a two-sided dispute begun just before this text.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 24-hour window is measured from the time of setting aside (הנחה).

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: the checking view fits well
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'he worries מעת לעת' and notes that they fit the view that counts from the checking.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: If they were lost, he must worry for 24 hours. Granted, for the one who counts the 24 hours from the checking, this works well.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge. First it shows that the משנה's wording fits one view nicely, so that it can next show the problem for the other view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the 24 hours are counted back from the checking, then 'he worries מעת לעת' means exactly that: he worries about one full day before the check. The wording matches with no extra words needed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We learned' (in a משנה); introduces a quote from a משנה
'Granted' or 'it works out for'; sets up a contrast with a view that has a problem

phrases.english: We learned in the משנה: If they were lost –
phrases.notes: 'They' means the produce or money he had set aside to rely on.

phrases.english: he must be concerned for a 24-hour period.
Granted, according to the one who said
a 24-hour period counted from the checking – it works well;

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: אִם אָבְדוּ הֲרֵי זֶה חוֹשֵׁשׁ מֵעֵת לְעֵת בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the two views from step 1 against the wording of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that counts from הנחה (set up here, attacked in step 3).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: First shows that the wording fits the בדיקה view, to set up the contrast.

steps.title: The setting-aside view does not match the משנה's wording
steps.stepSummary: For the view that counts from the setting aside, the משנה should have said 'until מעת לעת'. The challenge is left unanswered.
steps.simpleTranslation: But for the one who counts the 24 hours from the setting aside, does the משנה really say 'for 24 hours'? It should have said 'back until the point 24 hours after setting it aside'! This is a difficulty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the הנחה view because the משנה's words do not match it. It ends with 'קשיא', meaning the problem stays unsolved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the הנחה view, the worry goes back from the checking all the way until 24 hours after the setting aside, which is not just one day. So the משנה should have written 'עד מעת לעת'. Saying 'קשיא' does not cancel this view. It only marks the wording as a real difficulty for it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It should have said'; points out that the wording is not what we would expect
'Until'; here it would mark how far back the worry reaches
'It is difficult'; the challenge is left without an answer

steps.confusionAlert: 'קשיא' at the end is not the same as 'תיובתא'. It means the גמרא has no answer to the wording problem right now. It does not mean the view has been completely knocked down.

phrases.english: But according to the one who said
a 24-hour period counted from the setting aside –
is this 'for a 24-hour period'?!
It should have said 'until the 24-hour point'!
It is difficult.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מֵעֵת לְעֵת שֶׁל הַנָּחָה הַאי מֵעֵת לְעֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the contrast set up by 'בשלמא' in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that counts the 24 hours from הנחה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that view the worry stretches from the checking back to 24 hours after the setting aside. That needs the word 'עד', and the משנה does not say it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The wording of the משנה remains a difficulty for the הנחה view.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's colleagues disagree with him
steps.stepSummary: Quoting the words 'דברי רבי אלעזר' from the משנה, the אמורא רבי אלעזר says that the תנא רבי אלעזר's colleagues disagree with his 24-hour rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says this is 'the words of רבי אלעזר'. רבי אלעזר said: His colleagues disagree with רבי אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next words of the משנה, 'דברי רבי אלעזר'. An אמורא tells us that the other תנאים did not accept this 24-hour limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה named רבי אלעזר as the author of the 24-hour rule, and this hints that not everyone agrees. The אמורא רבי אלעזר states this outright: his colleagues are stricter and would make him worry further back.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The words of'; marks a ruling as one particular sage's view
His colleagues, the other sages of his generation

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different people named רבי אלעזר here. One is the תנא in the משנה who made the 24-hour rule. The other is the later אמורא who comments that the תנא's colleagues disagree.

phrases.english: 'The words of רבי אלעזר':
רבי אלעזר said:

phrases.aramaic: חֲלוּקִין עָלָיו חֲבֵירָיו עַל רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר –
phrases.english: His colleagues disagree with him, with רבי אלעזר –

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the counting dispute behind and turns to a new phrase of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The other תנאים do not accept רבי אלעזר's 24-hour limit.

steps.title: Proof from a מקוה found lacking
steps.stepSummary: A משנה rules that when a מקוה is measured and found short, everything purified in it is impure going all the way back. There is no 24-hour limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: A מקוה was measured and found to be lacking. All the pure items that were made pure in it, going back in time, are impure, whether in a private area or in a public area.
steps.whatsHappening: The אמורא brings a משנה to show that other sages do not limit the worry to 24 hours. With the מקוה, the worry goes all the way back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the מקוה is found lacking, all purifications done in it back to the last time it was known to be full are treated as impure. That is the opposite of רבי אלעזר's approach, where you only worry about 24 hours. The ruling applies in both a private and a public place.

keyTerms.meaning: A ritual bath, which needs a minimum amount of water to purify
Pure items, things handled or purified in purity
Going back in time, applying to the past

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר limits the worry to 24 hours. The מקוה משנה shows the other sages worry all the way back to the last time things were known to be fine.

phrases.english: As we learned: A מקוה that was measured
and was found lacking;

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל טְהָרוֹת שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ עַל גַּבָּיו לְמַפְרֵעַ –
phrases.english: all pure items that were made pure through it, going back in time –

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד, בֵּין בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים – טְמֵאוֹת.
phrases.english: whether in a private domain or in a public domain – are impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the claim in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אלעזר's colleagues disagree with his 24-hour limit.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in מקוואות: a מקוה found lacking makes all purifications done in it impure going back in time, in both private and public domains.

steps.title: Isn't it obvious that they disagree?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר the אמורא: the מקוה משנה obviously disagrees with the 24-hour rule, so why did he need to say it?
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious that they disagree!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי אלעזר the אמורא added. The מקוה משנה from Step 5 clearly makes everything impure 'למפרע', so of course it disagrees with the 24-hour rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 showed a משנה that makes things impure all the way back, with no 24-hour limit. If that is so plain, the אמורא's statement looks unnecessary. The גמרא wants to know what new point he is teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious, so why say it?

phrases.english: It is obvious that they disagree!
phrases.notes: He means the rabbis of the מקוה משנה obviously disagree with the תנא רבי אלעזר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the statement in Step 4, given the proof in Step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The statement of the אמורא רבי אלעזר that the colleagues disagree
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says 'למפרע' with no limit, so the disagreement is obvious and needs no statement.

steps.title: We might have thought 'retroactive' means 24 hours
steps.stepSummary: We could have read 'למפרע' as only going back 24 hours, so רבי אלעזר teaches that it really goes back further and they truly disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: what does 'retroactively' mean? Only 24 hours back. So he teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Without רבי אלעזר's statement, we might have thought the word 'למפרע' in the מקוה משנה only means 24 hours back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'למפרע' alone does not say how far back. One could read it as agreeing with the תנא רבי אלעזר's 24-hour window. The אמורא teaches that it means all the way back, so the two views really disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (a mistaken idea)

steps.whatToRemember: The rabbis of the מקוה משנה really disagree with רבי אלעזר's 24-hour rule. Their 'למפרע' goes further back than 24 hours.

phrases.english: You might have said:
What is 'retroactively'? 24 hours back,
so he teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the statement is needed to block a possible reading of the word 'למפרע'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'למפרע' might have meant only 24 hours back, in agreement with רבי אלעזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'למפרע' means all the way back, so the rabbis disagree with רבי אלעזר.

steps.title: Which east wind after סוכות
steps.stepSummary: On רבי יהודה's three checking times, a ברייתא explains that the east wind after סוכות counts only when it comes in its proper autumn season.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: רבי יהודה says, at three times and so on. A ברייתא taught: when the east wind blows after the festival in its season.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new part of the משנה, רבי יהודה's three times for checking wine. A ברייתא explains which east wind after סוכות is meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One of רבי יהודה's times is when the east wind blows after סוכות. The ברייתא adds 'של תקופה', meaning the normal autumn season of תשרי. This narrows the rule to the usual case.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה פְּרָקִים כּוּ׳:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says, at three times, etc.:
A Sage taught:
With the east wind at the end of the festival
of the season.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: בְּקִידּוּם שֶׁל מוֹצָאֵי הַחַג שֶׁל תְּקוּפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The east wind after סוכות means the one that comes in its usual autumn season.

steps.title: Three times for selling grain and wine, and oil after שבועות
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי יהודה lists the times of year when grain, wine and oil are sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: grain is sold at three times: before sowing, during sowing, and shortly before פסח. Wine is sold at three times: shortly before פסח, shortly before שבועות, and shortly before סוכות. Oil is sold from שבועות on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related ברייתא from רבי יהודה about set times for selling produce. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the three checking times in the משנה, רבי יהודה gives fixed seasons for selling grain and wine. Oil gets one starting point, from שבועות on. The ברייתא does not yet say what these times matter for.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
At three times one sells the grain:
before sowing, and at the time of sowing,
and shortly before Passover.
And at three times one sells the wine:
shortly before Passover, and shortly before Shavuot,
and shortly before the festival.
And oil: from Shavuot onward.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה פְּרָקִים מוֹכְרִין אֶת הַתְּבוּאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related list of three set times, this time for selling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Grain and wine each have three selling times; oil is sold from שבועות on.

steps.title: What are these selling times for?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical law the ברייתא's selling times are teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what law was this said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the selling times matter at all. Normally an owner can sell his produce whenever he wants.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A list of selling times seems pointless if anyone may sell any time. So it must be teaching a specific law, and the גמרא asks what it is.

phrases.english: For what law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the ברייתא in Step 9 is for.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical law depends on these selling times

steps.title: The rule is for partners
steps.stepSummary: רבא (or רב פפא) explains that the times matter for partners: at these times one partner may sell without asking the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said, and some say it was רב פפא: it is for partners.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that these times apply to business partners. At these seasons one partner may sell the shared produce on his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One partner usually cannot sell shared goods without the other's agreement. But at the usual selling seasons it is understood that selling is expected. So the list tells us when a partner may sell alone.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (it was someone else)

phrases.english: Rava said, and some say Rav Pappa:
For partners.
phrases.notes: At these times one partner may sell without the other's permission.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב פָּפָּא: לְשׁוּתָּפִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The selling times tell when one partner may sell without the other's permission.

steps.title: What about after the last selling time?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the law is once the last of the listed times has passed.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here on, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question. What happens after the last selling season has gone by?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a partner did not sell at the listed times, maybe he must now wait for next year or ask permission. The גמרא wants to know how the rule works after those times.

phrases.english: From here onward, what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follow-up question on the partners' rule in Step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The law after the last listed selling time has passed

steps.title: After that, every day is a selling time
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that once the last listed time has passed, any day is a proper time to sell.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: every day is its time.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers that after the listed times, the produce may be sold on any day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the main seasons are over, the produce is already overdue for selling. So a partner may sell it any day without waiting.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה's selling times are for partners. At those times, and any day after the last of them, one partner may sell alone.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Every day is its time.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: כׇּל יוֹמָא פִּירְקֵיהּ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: After the last listed time, any day is a proper selling time.

steps.title: What does 'חרישית' mean?
steps.stepSummary: Because the east wind came up, the גמרא quotes a פסוק in יונה about an east wind and asks what the word 'חרישית' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And when the sun rose, God prepared a חרישית east wind.' What does 'חרישית' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: Since the east wind came up in the משנה, the גמרא quotes a פסוק about an east wind. It asks about one unclear word, and the answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a side topic connected only by the east wind. The word 'חרישית' is unusual, so the גמרא asks what it describes.

keyTerms.meaning: An unusual word describing the wind

phrases.english: "And it was, when the sun rose,
that God prepared a charishit east wind"
What is "charishit"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Side topic linked to the east wind of Step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word 'חרישית' in the פסוק

steps.title: A wind that plows furrows in the sea
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that 'חרישית' comes from plowing: when the wind blows, it makes furrows in the sea.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: when it blows, it makes furrow after furrow in the sea.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers that 'חרישית' means plowing. The wind is so strong it cuts lines in the water like a plow in a field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word is linked to חרישה, plowing. The wind's power makes deep rows of waves, like furrows.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
When it blows,
it makes furrow after furrow in the sea.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'חרישית' means a plowing wind that makes furrows in the sea.

steps.title: רבה questions the plowing explanation
steps.stepSummary: רבה argues against רב יהודה's 'plowing' explanation from the rest of the פסוק in יונה, which describes heat, not strength.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to him: If so, is that what is written: 'And the sun beat on the head of יונה and he fainted'?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה pushes back on רב יהודה. If חרישית means a strong wind that plows the sea, why does the פסוק go on to describe a hot sun that made יונה faint?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה's reading stresses how strong the wind was. The end of the פסוק stresses heat. So the 'plowing' reading does not fit the context.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if your explanation is right)

phrases.english: Rabba said to him:
If so, is this what is written:
'And the sun beat on the head of Jonah
and he fainted'?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation given in step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's explanation that חרישית comes from plowing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The end of the פסוק describes heat, but a plowing wind is about strength, so the explanation does not fit the context.

steps.title: רבה: the east wind silences all other winds
steps.stepSummary: רבה gives a new explanation: חרישית means the wind makes all the other winds go silent.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבה said: At the time that it blows, it silences all the winds before it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה replaces רב יהודה's answer with his own. The east wind is called חרישית because when it blows, every other wind goes quiet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reads חרישית as coming from 'silence' rather than 'plowing.' With only this wind blowing, things get very hot, which fits the sun beating on יונה.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabba said:
At the time that it blows,
it silences all the winds before it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a replacement answer after the challenge in step 16
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It comes from silencing: the east wind quiets all other winds.

steps.title: A פסוק in איוב supports רבה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק in איוב that links heat to the land being made still by a wind.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what is written: 'You whose garments are hot, when the earth is still by reason of the south wind.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רבה with a פסוק. It connects hot clothing to a time when the earth is made still by a wind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links heat to stillness. That matches רבה's idea that when one wind silences the others, it becomes hot.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what is written

phrases.english: And this is what is written:
'You whose garments are hot,
when the earth is still by reason of the south wind.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבה's explanation
steps.raayaObject: The idea that one wind silences the others and causes heat

steps.title: רב חסדא explains the פסוק in איוב
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that clothes feel hottest when the south wind blows, because it silences every other wind.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי תחליפא בר רב חסדא said that רב חסדא said: When are your garments hot? When the earth is stilled by the south wind. For when it blows, it silences all the winds before it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא reads the פסוק the way רבה's idea needs. The greatest heat comes when one wind blows and quiets all the others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows the פסוק really means what step 18 used it for. The same 'silences all the winds' wording from רבה appears here, now said about the south wind.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי תַּחְלִיפָא בַּר רַב חִסְדָּא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Tachalifa bar Rav Chisda said,
Rav Chisda said:
When are your garments hot?
At the time when the earth is stilled by the south wind.
For at the time that it blows,
it silences all the winds before it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי תַּחְלִיפָא בַּר רַב חִסְדָּא, אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the פסוק cited in step 18
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Garments are hottest when the south wind blows, because it silences all other winds.
steps.whatToRemember: חרישית is explained in two ways: 'plowing' (רב יהודה) and 'silencing the other winds' (רבה). The second fits the heat described in יונה and the פסוק in איוב.

steps.title: Should they stand up for גניבא?
steps.stepSummary: While רב הונא and רב חסדא are sitting, גניבא passes by. One wants to stand for him as a Torah scholar; the other objects that he is a quarrelsome person.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא and רב חסדא were sitting. גניבא passed by them. One said to the other: Let us stand before him, for he is a Torah scholar. The other said to him: Shall we stand before a quarrelsome person?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story connected to the topic of winds. Two great scholars disagree about whether to stand up for גניבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One scholar looks at גניבא's Torah learning. The other looks at his quarrelsome behavior. The story sets up the Torah teaching about winds that גניבא is about to share.

keyTerms.meaning: Geneiva, a scholar of that time

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא וְרַב חִסְדָּא הֲווֹ יָתְבִי.
phrases.english: Rav Huna and Rav Chisda were sitting.
Geneiva was passing by them,
One said to the other:
Let us stand before him, for he is a Torah scholar.
The other said to him:
Shall we stand before a quarrelsome person?!
phrases.notes: פלגאה comes from 'split': someone who causes division and arguments.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא וְרַב חִסְדָּא הֲווֹ יָתְבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a story that leads into more teaching about winds
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A story: the two scholars disagree about whether to stand for גניבא.

steps.title: גניבא asks what they were learning
steps.stepSummary: Meanwhile, גניבא comes over and asks what they were learning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Meanwhile, he came to them and said to them: With what were you occupied?
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves forward: גניבא joins them and asks about their topic. This sets up his teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is only a transition. The question opens the door for גניבא to share a teaching on their subject.

phrases.english: Meanwhile, he came to them,
he said to them: With what were you occupied?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What topic were the scholars learning?

steps.title: They were learning about winds
steps.stepSummary: They answer that they were learning about winds.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: About winds.
steps.whatsHappening: The scholars tell גניבא their topic was winds. This prepares for his teaching in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ties the story back to the topic the גמרא was discussing in the steps before.

phrases.english: They said to him: About winds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers גניבא's question

steps.title: Four winds blow every day, and the north wind blows with all of them
steps.stepSummary: גניבא quotes רב: all four winds blow each day, and the north wind blows together with each one. Without it, the world could not last even an hour.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Thus said רב חנן בר רבא in the name of רב: Four winds blow every day, and the north wind blows with all of them; for if not, the world would not survive even one hour.
steps.whatsHappening: גניבא shares a teaching in רב's name about how the winds blow. The north wind joins every other wind and keeps the world going.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new point is that the north wind is always present, blowing together with each of the other winds. Without it, the world could not last even one hour.

phrases.english: He said to them:

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי אָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר רָבָא,
phrases.english: Thus said Rav Chanan bar Rava,
Rav said:
Four winds blow every day,
and the north wind blows together with all of them;
for if it were not so,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין הָעוֹלָם מִתְקַיֵּים אֲפִילּוּ שָׁעָה אַחַת.
phrases.english: the world would not survive even one hour.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר רָבָא, אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: גניבא's teaching on the topic of winds
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All four winds blow daily, and the north wind accompanies each one so the world can survive.

steps.title: The south wind is the harshest, held back by בן נץ
steps.stepSummary: The south wind is the harshest of all. If בן נץ did not hold it back, it would destroy the whole world.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the south wind is the harshest of all, and if not for בן נץ holding it back, it would destroy the entire world before it.
steps.whatsHappening: The teaching continues: the south wind is the most dangerous, and something called בן נץ keeps it in check.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The north wind protects the world, and the south wind threatens it. A פסוק will be brought next to show where בן נץ comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: Ben Netz, the force that holds back the south wind

phrases.english: And the south wind is the harshest of all,
and if not for Ben Netz holding it back,
phrases.notes: בן נץ is understood as an angel. The name comes from נץ, the hawk in the פסוק coming next.

phrases.english: it would destroy the entire world before it,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues גניבא's teaching
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The south wind is the harshest and would destroy the world if בן נץ did not hold it back.

steps.title: The hawk spreading its wings to the south
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in איוב about a hawk (נץ) spreading its wings toward the south is the source for בן נץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is said: 'Does the hawk soar by your wisdom, spreading its wings toward the south?'
steps.whatsHappening: The teaching brings a פסוק to support the idea of בן נץ. The פסוק mentions a נץ and the south.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק joins the word נץ with תימן (south). That is the link to a force called בן נץ that stands against the south wind.

phrases.english: As it is said: 'Does the hawk soar by your wisdom,
spreading its wings toward the south?'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for בן נץ
steps.raayaObject: That בן נץ holds back the south wind
steps.whatToRemember: The north wind blows with every wind and protects the world. The south wind is the harshest and is held back by בן נץ.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יעקב passes by in a golden carriage
steps.stepSummary: A new story: רבא and רב נחמן בר יצחק are sitting when רב נחמן בר יעקב passes by in a golden carriage, covered with a green cloak.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא and רב נחמן בר יצחק were sitting; רב נחמן בר יעקב was passing by, sitting in a golden carriage with a green cloak spread over him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a second story about scholars sitting and someone passing by. This step sets the scene for what happens next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the גניבא story, this one is about how scholars react to someone who passes by. The fancy carriage and cloak will matter for רב נחמן בר יצחק's reasoning.

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא וְרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק הֲווֹ יָתְבִי;
phrases.english: Rava and Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak were sitting;

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה חָלֵיף וְאָזֵיל רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יַעֲקֹב,
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yaakov was passing by,
sitting in a golden carriage
with a green cloak spread over him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא וְרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק הֲווֹ יָתְבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story, similar in setting to the story of גניבא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Scene setting: רב נחמן בר יעקב passes by in a showy carriage.

steps.title: One goes over to him, one stays put
steps.stepSummary: רבא goes over to רב נחמן בר יעקב, but רב נחמן בר יצחק does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא went over to him; רב נחמן בר יצחק did not go over to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The two scholars react differently. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the story only tells us what each one did. The reason for רב נחמן בר יצחק's choice comes in the next step.

phrases.english: Rava went over to him,

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק לָא אֲזַל לְגַבֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak did not go over to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא approached, רב נחמן בר יצחק did not.

steps.title: Why רב נחמן בר יצחק did not go
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that the riders might be from the household of the ראש גלותא. רבא needs them, but he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Perhaps they are people of the ראש גלותא's household; רבא needs them, I do not need them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains why he stayed seated. He thought the riders might belong to the ראש גלותא's household, and he had no need of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He did not recognize the rider as a scholar. He assumed it was someone from the ruling household. Going over to such people made sense for רבא, who needed them, but not for himself.

keyTerms.meaning: The household of the Exilarch (leader of the Jews in Babylonia)

phrases.english: He said: Perhaps they are from the people
of the Exilarch's household;
Rava needs them,
I do not need them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר: דִּלְמָא מֵאִינָשֵׁי דְּבֵי רֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the behavior described in step 27
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן בר יצחק stayed seated because he thought the riders were officials of the ראש גלותא, whom he did not need.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק also goes over
steps.stepSummary: Once רב נחמן בר יצחק sees that the rider is רב נחמן בר יעקב, he also goes over to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he saw that it was רב נחמן בר יעקב, he went over to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. Now that רב נחמן בר יצחק knows the rider is a fellow scholar and not the ראש גלותא's men, he goes over too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the previous step he stayed back because he did not want to approach the ראש גלותא's officials. Once he sees it is really רב נחמן בר יעקב, a תלמיד חכם, he goes to greet him.

phrases.aramaic: כְּדַחֲזָא דְּרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יַעֲקֹב הֲוָה,
phrases.english: When he saw that it was Rav Nachman bar Yaakov,
phrases.notes: "He" here is רב נחמן בר יצחק, who had stayed behind before.

phrases.english: he went over to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדַחֲזָא דְּרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יַעֲקֹב הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the scene from step 28. His reason for holding back no longer applies, so he goes over.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once he knew the rider was רב נחמן בר יעקב, רב נחמן בר יצחק also went over to him.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יעקב feels the שַׁדְיָא wind
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יעקב uncovers his arm and says that the שַׁדְיָא wind is blowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: He uncovered his arm and said: The שַׁדְיָא wind is blowing!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יעקב feels a hot wind, bares his arm, and names it. This sets up the teachings that follow about this wind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line brings the story back to the main topic of winds, which ran from step 14 through step 25. Naming the wind gives רבא the opening to quote what the אמוראים said about it.

keyTerms.meaning: the name of a harmful hot wind

phrases.english: He uncovered his arm,
and said: Shadya is blowing!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story and leads into a teaching about the wind he names.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן בר יעקב identifies the wind blowing as שַׁדְיָא.

steps.title: Three opinions on the damage this wind causes
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes רב, who says a woman miscarries because of this wind. שמואל says even a pearl in the sea rots. רבי יוחנן says even seed inside a woman spoils.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said that רב said: A woman miscarries because of it. שמואל said: Even a pearl in the sea rots because of it. רבי יוחנן said: Even the seed inside a woman's body spoils because of it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא reports three statements about how harmful this wind is. Each one names a different kind of damage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each view uses a stronger example of the wind's power. שמואל and רבי יוחנן both say "even" (אֲפִילּוּ): the wind reaches a pearl deep in the sea, or seed hidden inside the body. The three views do not seem to argue; each adds another example.

phrases.english: Rava said: This is what Rav said:
phrases.notes: "It" in these lines means the שַׁדְיָא wind.

phrases.english: A woman miscarries because of it;
And Shmuel said:
Even a pearl in the sea rots because of it;
Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ שִׁכְבַת זֶרַע שֶׁבִּמְעֵי אִשָּׁה מַסְרַחַת בּוֹ.
phrases.english: Even the seed inside a woman's body spoils because of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the wind has been named, רבא quotes earlier teachings about it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שַׁדְיָא wind causes miscarriage (רב), rots pearls in the sea (שמואל), and spoils seed in the womb (רבי יוחנן).

steps.title: All three opinions come from one verse
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק shows that all three statements come from one פסוק in הושע about the east wind. Each opinion matches a different phrase in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: All three learned it from one פסוק: "Though he be fruitful among the reed-plants, an east wind shall come, the wind of ה' coming up from the wilderness, and his spring shall become dry..." "His spring shall become dry" means a woman's womb. "And his fountain shall be dried up" means the seed inside a woman. "He shall spoil the treasure of all precious vessels" means a pearl in the sea.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives the source for the three statements. He matches each phrase of the פסוק to one of the three opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The "spring" (מָקוֹר) that dries up is the womb, which matches רב's miscarriage. The "fountain" (מַעְיָן) is the seed, which matches רבי יוחנן. The "treasure of precious vessels" is a pearl, which matches שמואל. So the three views are not three guesses; each one reads a different phrase of the same פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: they learned it from one פסוק

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that statements by different אמוראים which look unrelated can all come from close reading of one פסוק.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
And all three of them learned it from one verse:
"Though he be fruitful among the reed-plants,
phrases.notes: הושע 13:15. The גמרא asks what this opening phrase means in step 34.

phrases.english: an east wind shall come, the wind of the Lord
coming up from the wilderness,
and his spring shall become dry, etc."
"His spring shall become dry": this is a woman's womb.
"And his fountain shall be dried up":
this is the seed inside a woman's body.
"He shall spoil the treasure of all precious vessels":
this is a pearl in the sea.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source in the פסוק for the three statements in step 31.
steps.raayaObject: The three statements of רב, שמואל, and רבי יוחנן about the שַׁדְיָא wind.
steps.raayaSupportSource: הושע 13:15: "יָבוֹא קָדִים רוּחַ ה׳... וְיֵבוֹשׁ מְקוֹרוֹ וְיֶחֱרַב מַעְיָינוֹ הוּא יִשְׁסֶה אוֹצַר כׇּל כְּלִי חֶמְדָּה"

steps.title: רבא praises the precision of the Sura scholars
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that רב נחמן בר יצחק must be from סורא, because the scholars there read פסוקים very precisely.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This one is from סורא, for they are precise in reading פסוקים!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא reacts to the reading in step 32 with praise. He links this careful reading of the פסוק to the scholars of סורא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Matching every phrase of the פסוק to a separate idea is careful work. רבא sees this style as typical of סורא, the city of רב's yeshiva.

phrases.english: Rava said:
This one is from Sura,
phrases.notes: He means רב נחמן בר יצחק, who just explained the פסוק.

phrases.english: for they are precise in reading verses!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds with praise to the reading of the פסוק in step 32.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Careful phrase-by-phrase reading of פסוקים is typical of the scholars of סורא.

steps.title: What does "fruitful among the reed-plants" mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the opening words of the פסוק mean, "Though he be fruitful among the reed-plants." רבא begins to answer with "Even..."
steps.simpleTranslation: What does "Though he be fruitful among the reed-plants" mean? רבא said: Even...
steps.whatsHappening: So far only the second half of the פסוק has been explained, so the גמרא now asks about its first words. רבא starts to answer, and his answer continues in the text that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 32 explained only the parts of the פסוק about damage. This question fills in the opening phrase. רבא's "Even" signals that he will describe something that seems safe from the wind but is still harmed.

phrases.english: What does "Though he be fruitful among the reed-plants" mean?
Rava said: Even

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the פסוק from step 32 to explain the opening phrase that has not yet been explained.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the opening phrase "כִּי הוּא בֵּין אַחִים יַפְרִיא" in the context of the harmful wind.
